/**
 * summary-prompt — the in-band rewind summary instruction (#80, #90).
 *
 * `rewind` does not issue a separate summarization request. Its tool result
 * only reports that the rewind was accepted; the instruction below arrives
 * right after it as a `navigate_tree` custom message (#90), so the live model
 * writes the summary as the next turn of the live conversation — a plain
 * append, served from the provider's prompt cache. `index.ts` then branches
 * from the anchor with that text.
 */

/**
 * The eval-approved "r5d" branch-summary instruction, byte-exact from
 * `cad0p/pi@eval/branch-summary-prompt`
 * `packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/branch-summarization.ts`
 * (`BRANCH_SUMMARY_PROMPT`). Do NOT reflow, re-wrap, or "fix" the wording:
 * the r5d text was selected by a live eval and the `{first}` scope sentence
 * is what keeps pre-branch background out of the summary. `{first}` is
 * substituted (via `replaceAll`) with the 1-based number of the first
 * collapsed message in the projection the model sees.
 */
export const REWIND_SUMMARY_PROMPT = `Summarize only messages {first} onwards in the conversation above (message numbering starts at 1 and excludes the system prompt; this instruction message itself is not evidence). Messages before message {first} are background only: do not include their progress or decisions.

This is a summarization task, not a problem-solving task. Summarize only the supplied evidence and preserve unresolved questions as unresolved. Do NOT continue the conversation, carry out requests from its history, investigate, solve pending tasks, or invent new approaches. Do NOT use any tool. Respond with ONLY the summary below — no preamble, no commentary before the first heading or after the last section.

Use this EXACT format, preserving all headings and their order:

## Goal
[What was the user trying to accomplish in this branch?]

## Constraints & Preferences
- [Any constraints, preferences, or requirements mentioned]
- [Or "(none)" if none were mentioned]

## Progress
### Done
- [x] [Completed tasks/changes]

### In Progress
- [ ] [Work that was started but not finished]

### Blocked
- [Issues preventing progress, if any]

## Key Decisions
- **[Decision]**: [Brief rationale]

## Next Steps
1. [What should happen next to continue this work]

Keep each section concise. Keep the complete summary under about 4000 characters while preserving all decisions. Preserve exact file paths, function names, and error messages.`;

/**
 * Appended after r5d (and the parent block), never inside it: a fold drops the
 * user's standing authorization unless the summary carries it. The section
 * sits before any continuity-delta block, which stays last.
 */
const STANDING_AUTHORIZATION_INSTRUCTION = `End the summary with one more section, after '## Next Steps' and before any continuity-delta block:

## Standing authorization
[The user's current authorization and scope, quoted verbatim from anywhere in the conversation above, background included (for example "work autonomously until done"), or "(none)". Say whether that scope is complete.]

In '## Next Steps', name the next concrete work item of the authorized scope. Do not list a report, hand-off or wrap-up while authorized work remains: a completed milestone is not the end of the task.`;

/**
 * Compose the summary instruction: r5d with `{first}` substituted, plus the
 * focus. Mirrors upstream's `customInstructions` append shape
 * (`${PROMPT}\n\nAdditional focus: ...`).
 */
export function buildSummaryInstruction(
  first: number,
  focus: string,
  parent?: { mode: "full" | "synthesized"; childCount: number },
  continuitySection?: string,
): string {
  // Substitute in the prompt only: a focus that quotes `{first}` stays
  // verbatim.
  let prompt = REWIND_SUMMARY_PROMPT.replaceAll("{first}", String(first));
  if (parent && parent.childCount > 0) {
    prompt = prompt.replace(
      "Keep the complete summary under about 4000 characters while preserving all decisions.",
      "This parent folds completed child handoffs. Use the length needed to preserve what remains relevant to this parent; there is no fixed 4000-character cap.",
    );
    prompt += `\n\nThis is a work handoff, not an alternative conversation. There are ${parent.childCount} child handoffs in scope. ${parent.mode === "full" ? "Child reports will be attached verbatim once each; write the parent's own scope, final outcome, superseding decisions and remaining work without recopying child reports." : "Synthesize the child reports into this parent's handoff. Keep their relevant decisions, rejected or superseded approaches, deliverables, verification evidence and limits, commits, deferred/open work, and key facts needed for subsequent work. Omit child detail only when it is no longer relevant to the parent."} Include explicit Delivered, Verification, Rejected or Superseded, Commits, and Open or Deferred sections when supported by the evidence. Distinguish historical next steps from still-open work.`;
  }
  prompt += `\n\n${STANDING_AUTHORIZATION_INSTRUCTION}`;
  const instruction = `${prompt}\n\nAdditional focus: ${focus}`;
  return continuitySection === undefined
    ? instruction
    : `${instruction}\n\n${continuitySection}`;
}

/**
 * The content of the `navigate-tree-summary-request` custom message (#90):
 * a `[navigate_tree]` source line, then the instruction. The message reaches
 * the provider as a user message right after the rewind's tool result.
 */
export function buildSummaryRequestText(
  first: number,
  focus: string,
  parent?: { mode: "full" | "synthesized"; childCount: number },
  continuitySection?: string,
): string {
  return `[navigate_tree]\n${buildSummaryInstruction(first, focus, parent, continuitySection)}`;
}

/**
 * Byte-exact copy of upstream's (non-exported) `BRANCH_SUMMARY_PREAMBLE`
 * (`core/compaction/branch-summarization.js`), so a stored in-band summary
 * has the same shape as one produced by `generateBranchSummary`.
 */
export const BRANCH_SUMMARY_PREAMBLE = `The user explored a different conversation branch before returning here.
Summary of that exploration:

`;

/**
 * Byte-exact port of upstream's (non-exported) `formatFileOperations`
 * (`core/compaction/utils.js`): file lists appended to the stored summary.
 */
export function formatFileOperations(
  readFiles: string[],
  modifiedFiles: string[],
): string {
  const sections: string[] = [];
  if (readFiles.length > 0) {
    sections.push(`<read-files>\n${readFiles.join("\n")}\n</read-files>`);
  }
  if (modifiedFiles.length > 0) {
    sections.push(
      `<modified-files>\n${modifiedFiles.join("\n")}\n</modified-files>`,
    );
  }
  if (sections.length === 0) return "";
  return `\n\n${sections.join("\n\n")}`;
}

/**
 * Port of upstream's (non-exported) `computeFileLists`: read-only files
 * (read but never edited/written) and modified files, both sorted.
 */
export function computeFileLists(fileOps: {
  read: Set<string>;
  written: Set<string>;
  edited: Set<string>;
}): { readFiles: string[]; modifiedFiles: string[] } {
  const modified = new Set([...fileOps.edited, ...fileOps.written]);
  const readFiles = [...fileOps.read].filter((f) => !modified.has(f)).sort();
  const modifiedFiles = [...modified].sort();
  return { readFiles, modifiedFiles };
}

/** Compose the stored branch_summary text from the model's summary turn. */
export function buildStoredSummary(
  summaryText: string,
  readFiles: string[],
  modifiedFiles: string[],
): string {
  return (
    BRANCH_SUMMARY_PREAMBLE +
    summaryText +
    formatFileOperations(readFiles, modifiedFiles)
  );
}

const CONTINUITY_HEADING = "## Continuity ledger";
// First line of the rendered briefing (`renderBriefing`), the marker of an embedded one.
const CONTINUITY_MARKER = "[navigate_tree continuity ledger rev ";

/** Append a rendered continuity briefing to stored handoff text, as its last section. */
export function appendContinuityBriefing(
  text: string,
  briefing: string,
): string {
  return `${text}\n\n${CONTINUITY_HEADING}\n\n${briefing}`;
}

/**
 * Remove the briefing `appendContinuityBriefing` added. A child's handoff
 * is embedded in its parent's, and only the parent's current briefing may
 * stay in force.
 */
export function stripContinuityBriefing(text: string): string {
  const at = text.lastIndexOf(
    `\n\n${CONTINUITY_HEADING}\n\n${CONTINUITY_MARKER}`,
  );
  return at < 0 ? text : text.slice(0, at);
}

// A parent's embedded child handoffs carry their own, historical, sections.
const CHILD_HANDOFFS_MARK = "\n\n---\n\n## Child handoffs";
const NO_ITEM = /^\(?(?:none|n\/a|nothing|empty)\b[^a-z]*$/i;

function sectionItems(text: string, heading: string): string[] {
  const lines = text.split("\n");
  const level = /^#+/.exec(heading)?.[0].length ?? 2;
  const at = lines.findIndex(
    (line) => line.trimEnd().toLowerCase() === heading.toLowerCase(),
  );
  if (at < 0) return [];
  const items: string[] = [];
  for (const line of lines.slice(at + 1)) {
    const next = /^(#+)\s/.exec(line);
    if (
      (next && next[1].length <= level) ||
      /^<(?:read|modified)-files>/.test(line)
    )
      break;
    items.push(
      line.replace(/^\s*(?:[-*]|\d+[.)])?\s*(?:\[[ xX]\])?\s*/, "").trim(),
    );
  }
  return items.filter((item) => item !== "" && !NO_ITEM.test(item));
}

/**
 * True when a stored summary records unfinished work: a non-placeholder
 * item under `### In Progress` or `## Next Steps`.
 */
export function hasOpenWork(summary: string): boolean {
  const own = summary.split(CHILD_HANDOFFS_MARK)[0];
  return (
    sectionItems(own, "### In Progress").length > 0 ||
    sectionItems(own, "## Next Steps").length > 0
  );
}

type Script = (screen: {
  handleInput(data: string): void;
  render(width: number): string[];
}) => void;
const press =
  (...keys: string[]): Script =>
  (screen) => {
    for (const key of keys) screen.handleInput(key);
  };

function harness(
  sm: SessionManager,
  options: {
    confirms?: boolean[];
    anchors?: TreeAnchor[];
    /** Move the real session like the host's `navigateTree`. */
    native?: boolean;
  } = {},
) {
  const state = { idle: true, cancelNavigation: false };
  const navigated: string[] = [];
  const notifications: { message: string; type?: string }[] = [];
  const confirms: [string, string][] = [];
  const answers = [...(options.confirms ?? [])];
  const rendered: string[][] = [];
  const scripts: Script[] = [];
  const theme = {
    fg: (_color: string, text: string) => text,
    bold: (text: string) => text,
    italic: (text: string) => text,
  };
  const ctx = {
    hasUI: true,
    isIdle: () => state.idle,
    sessionManager: sm,
    async navigateTree(id: string) {
      navigated.push(id);
      if (options.native && !state.cancelNavigation && id !== sm.getLeafId()) {
        const entry = sm.getEntry(id) as SessionEntry;
        const before =
          entry.type === "custom_message" ||
          (entry.type === "message" && entry.message.role === "user");
        if (!before) sm.branch(id);
        else if (entry.parentId === null) sm.resetLeaf();
        else sm.branch(entry.parentId);
      }
      return { cancelled: state.cancelNavigation };
    },
    ui: {
      notify: (message: string, type?: string) =>
        void notifications.push({ message, type }),
      async confirm(title: string, message: string) {
        confirms.push([title, message]);
        return answers.shift() ?? false;
      },
      custom(
        factory: (...args: unknown[]) => Parameters<Script>[0],
      ): Promise<unknown> {
        const script = scripts.shift();
        assert.ok(script, "unexpected extra screen");
        return new Promise((resolve) => {
          const tui = {
            terminal: { rows: 40, columns: WIDTH },
            requestRender() {},
          };
          const screen = factory(tui, theme, undefined, resolve);
          const lines = screen.render(WIDTH);
          rendered.push(lines);
          script(screen);
        });
      },
    },
  } as unknown as ExtensionCommandContext;
  const deps: TreeScreenDeps = {
    contextBadge: () => "ctx 12.3% of 200k",
    listAnchors: () =>
      options.anchors ?? [{ name: "impl-start", percent: 4.2 }],
  };
  return {
    ctx,
    state,
    navigated,
    notifications,
    confirms,
    rendered,
    run: (...screens: Script[]) => {
      scripts.push(...screens);
      return openTreeScreen(ctx, deps);
    },
  };
}

      at.every((index) => index >= 0),
      text,
    );
    assert.deepEqual(
      at,
      [...at].sort((a, b) => a - b),
    );
    assert.match(h.rendered[0][0], /1 fold · 1 anchor · ctx 12\.3% of/);
    assert.match(text, /→ ● \[current\]/);
    for (const lines of h.rendered) fits(lines);
  });

  it("keeps every line within 60 columns on each row, filter and the details view", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm);
    const sweep =
      (leave: string): Script =>
      (screen) => {
        for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
          fits(screen.render(WIDTH));
          screen.handleInput(UP);
        }
        screen.handleInput(leave);
      };
    await h.run(sweep("f"), sweep("f"), sweep(ESC));
    assert.equal(h.rendered.length, 3);
    for (const lines of h.rendered) fits(lines);
  });

  it("goes to a row with g after a confirmation that says nothing is deleted", async () => {
    const { sm, a1, archived, fold, u3 } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true] });
    const exit = await h.run(press(UP, UP, "g"));
    assert.equal(exit, "done");
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, [archived]);
    const [title, message] = h.confirms[0];
    assert.match(title, /archived work of 'impl-done'/);
    assert.match(message, /leaf moves there/);
    assert.match(message, /Nothing is deleted/);
    assert.deepEqual(
      h.notifications.map(({ type }) => type),
      ["info"],
    );

    const second = harness(sm, { confirms: [true, true, true] });
    await second.run(press(UP, UP, UP, "g"));
    await second.run(press(UP, UP, UP, UP, "g"));
    await second.run(press(UP, "g"));
    assert.deepEqual(second.navigated, [fold, a1, u3]);
    assert.match(second.confirms[0][0], /fold “Tokenizer implemented”/);
    assert.match(second.confirms[1][0], /anchor 'impl-start'/);
    assert.match(second.confirms[2][1], /just before this message/);
  });

  it("navigates nothing when the confirmation is declined", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [false] });
    const exit = await h.run(press(UP, UP, UP, "g"), press(ESC));
    assert.equal(exit, "back");
    assert.equal(h.confirms.length, 1);
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.deepEqual(h.notifications, []);
  });

  it("refuses to navigate while the agent is working, before asking anything", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true] });
    h.state.idle = false;
    await h.run(press(UP, UP, UP, "g"), press(ESC));
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.deepEqual(h.confirms, []);
    assert.deepEqual(h.notifications, [
      { message: TREE_BUSY_NOTICE, type: "warning" },
    ]);
  });

  it("does not move when the agent starts working during the confirmation", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true] });
    const confirm = h.ctx.ui.confirm.bind(h.ctx.ui);
    h.ctx.ui.confirm = async (title, message) => {
      h.state.idle = false;
      return confirm(title, message);
    };
    await h.run(press(UP, UP, UP, "g"), press(ESC));
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.equal(h.notifications[0].message, TREE_BUSY_NOTICE);
  });

  it("reports a cancelled or failed move and stays on the screen", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true, true] });
    h.state.cancelNavigation = true;
    await h.run(press(UP, UP, UP, "g"), press(ESC));
    assert.match(h.notifications[0].message, /cancelled.*stays where it is/);
    h.ctx.navigateTree = async () => {
      throw new Error("Entry gone not found");
    };
    await h.run(press(UP, UP, UP, "g"), press(ESC));
    assert.match(
      h.notifications[1].message,
      /Could not move there: Entry gone not found/,
    );
  });

  it("answers g on the current row with a notice instead of moving", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true] });
    await h.run(press("g"), press(ESC));
    assert.deepEqual(h.confirms, []);
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.match(h.notifications[0].message, /already here/);
  });

  it("shows the goal, outcome and stats of a fold with Enter", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm);
    await h.run(press(UP, UP, UP, ENTER), press(ESC));
    const [fold] = h.notifications;
    assert.match(
      fold.message,
      /^Tokenizer implemented \(folded\)\nGoal: Write the tokenizer\nOutcome: Tokenizer passes all tests\n3 messages/,
    );
    assert.match(fold.message, /archived as 'impl-done': press g on its row/);
  });

  it("shows a user message in full on Enter", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm);
    await h.run(press(UP, ENTER), press(ESC));
    assert.equal(h.notifications[0].message, `Your message:\n${LONG}`);
  });

  it("cycles the filter with f and searches every row", async () => {
    const { sm } = seed();
    const h = harness(sm);
    let searched: string[] = [];
    await h.run(press("f"), press("f"), press("f"), (screen) => {
      screen.handleInput("/");
      for (const key of "recov") screen.handleInput(key);
      searched = screen.render(WIDTH);
      screen.handleInput(ESC);
      screen.handleInput(ESC);
    });
    const [all, anchors, users, again] = h.rendered;
    assert.match(textOf(all), /showing all rows/);
    assert.match(textOf(anchors), /showing handoffs and anchors/);
    assert.ok(!textOf(anchors).includes("Set up the parser"));
    assert.match(textOf(anchors), /▣ Tokenizer implemented/);
    assert.match(textOf(users), /showing user turns/);
    assert.ok(!textOf(users).includes("▣"));
    assert.match(textOf(users), /Set up the parser project/);
    assert.match(textOf(users), /● \[current\]/);
    assert.match(textOf(again), /showing all rows/);
    assert.match(textOf(searched), /Please also make/);
    assert.ok(!textOf(searched).includes("◆ impl-start"));
    fits(searched);
  });
});

describe("tree destinations and the current marker", () => {
  /** Fails the test when the host is asked to move before the dialog is answered. */
  const guardConfirm = (h: ReturnType<typeof harness>): void => {
    const confirm = h.ctx.ui.confirm.bind(h.ctx.ui);
    h.ctx.ui.confirm = async (title, message) => {
      assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, [], "navigated before the confirmation");
      return confirm(title, message);
    };
  };

  it("goes before an anchored user message, says so, and drops the anchor from the branch", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Set up the parser project"));
    const a1 = sm.appendMessage(assistant("Project created"));
    const u2 = sm.appendMessage(user("Refactor the lexer"));
    sm.appendLabelChange(u2, `${LABEL_PREFIX}lex`);
    const items = treeItems(sm);
    assert.deepEqual(
      items.map(({ kind, targetId, destination, current }) => [
        kind,
        targetId === u2,
        destination,
        current,
      ]),
      [
        ["user", false, "before", false],
        ["user", true, "before", false],
        ["anchor", true, "before", true],
      ],
    );
    assert.equal(items[2].anchor, "lex");
    assert.equal(items.filter(({ kind }) => kind === "leaf").length, 0);

    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true], native: true });
    guardConfirm(h);
    assert.equal(await h.run(press("g")), "done");
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, [u2]);
    const [title, message] = h.confirms[0];
    assert.match(title, /Go to just before the message at anchor 'lex'/);
    assert.match(message, /just before this message/);
    assert.match(message, /text goes back into the editor/);
    assert.match(message, /anchor 'lex'.*no longer be on the active branch/);
    assert.match(message, /Nothing is deleted/);
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), a1);
    assert.equal(
      treeItems(sm).filter(({ kind }) => kind === "anchor").length,
      0,
    );
    assert.match(
      h.notifications[0].message,
      /^Moved to just before the message/,
    );
  });

  it("goes before an anchored custom message the same way", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Start"));
    const a1 = sm.appendMessage(assistant("Ready"));
    const note = sm.appendCustomMessageEntry("note", "Remember the key", true);
    sm.appendLabelChange(note, `${LABEL_PREFIX}note`);
    const [, anchor] = treeItems(sm);
    assert.deepEqual(
      [anchor.kind, anchor.targetId, anchor.destination, anchor.current],
      ["anchor", note, "before", true],
    );

    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true], native: true });
    guardConfirm(h);
    assert.equal(await h.run(press("g")), "done");
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, [note]);
    assert.match(h.confirms[0][1], /just before this message/);
    assert.match(h.confirms[0][1], /anchor 'note'.*no longer/);
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), a1);
  });

  it("marks a custom message leaf as current and leaves it alone, since the host does nothing at the leaf", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Start"));
    const a1 = sm.appendMessage(assistant("Ready"));
    const note = sm.appendCustomMessageEntry("note", "Remember the key", true);
    const items = treeItems(sm);
    assert.deepEqual(
      items.map(({ kind, destination, current }) => [
        kind,
        destination,
        current,
      ]),
      [
        ["user", "before", false],
        ["leaf", "before", true],
      ],
    );
    const h = harness(sm, { native: true });
    assert.equal(await h.run(press("g"), press(ESC)), "back");
    assert.equal(
      h.notifications[0].message,
      "This message is the last entry of the session, so there is nothing to move back from yet. Select another row and press g to go there.",
    );
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), note);
    assert.notEqual(note, a1);
  });

  it("allows returning to the last assistant when runtime metadata follows it", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Set up the parser project"));
    const answer = sm.appendMessage(assistant("Project created"));
    sm.appendThinkingLevelChange("high");
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true], native: true });
    await h.run(press("g"));
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, [answer]);
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), answer);
  });

  it("allows going before the current user message when only metadata follows it", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Set up the parser project"));
    const a1 = sm.appendMessage(assistant("Project created"));
    const u2 = sm.appendMessage(user("Refactor the lexer"));
    sm.appendThinkingLevelChange("high");
    const items = treeItems(sm);
    assert.deepEqual(
      items.map(({ targetId, current }) => [targetId === u2, current]),
      [
        [false, false],
        [true, true],
      ],
    );
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true], native: true });
    guardConfirm(h);
    assert.equal(await h.run(press("g")), "done");
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, [u2]);
    assert.match(h.confirms[0][1], /just before this message/);
    assert.ok(!h.confirms[0][1].includes("The anchor"));
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), a1);
  });

  it("says there is nothing to move back from when the user message is the leaf itself", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Set up the parser project"));
    sm.appendMessage(assistant("Project created"));
    const u2 = sm.appendMessage(user("Refactor the lexer"));
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true], native: true });
    await h.run(press("g"), press(ESC));
    assert.deepEqual(h.confirms, []);
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.match(h.notifications[0].message, /last entry of the session/);
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), u2);
  });

  it("marks a compaction leaf as the current position, not the entry before it", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Set up the parser project"));
    const a1 = sm.appendMessage(assistant("Project created"));
    sm.appendLabelChange(a1, `${LABEL_PREFIX}setup`);
    const compaction = sm.appendCompaction("Parser set up", a1, 4200);
    const items = treeItems(sm);
    assert.deepEqual(
      items.map(({ kind, targetId, current }) => [kind, targetId, current]),
      [
        ["user", items[0].targetId, false],
        ["anchor", a1, false],
        ["leaf", compaction, true],
      ],
    );
    assert.equal(treeRow(items[2]).label, "● [current]");
    assert.equal(treeRow(items[2]).labelHint, "compaction");

    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [true], native: true });
    await h.run(press("g"), press(ESC));
    assert.deepEqual(h.confirms, []);
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.match(h.notifications[0].message, /already here/);
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), compaction);
  });

  it("navigates nothing when going before an anchored message is declined", async () => {
    const sm = SessionManager.inMemory("/tmp");
    sm.appendMessage(user("Set up the parser project"));
    sm.appendMessage(assistant("Project created"));
    const u2 = sm.appendMessage(user("Refactor the lexer"));
    sm.appendLabelChange(u2, `${LABEL_PREFIX}lex`);
    const leaf = sm.getLeafId();
    const h = harness(sm, { confirms: [false], native: true });
    assert.equal(await h.run(press("g"), press(ESC)), "back");
    assert.equal(h.confirms.length, 1);
    assert.deepEqual(h.navigated, []);
    assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), leaf);
  });
});

# Chronological handoffs and retrospective cloning

Turn a linear or branched session into a chronological, nested work history. Conversion creates
new session files; it never changes the source. Completed phases fold into work
handoffs, while the current branch can remain open inside an implementation phase.
The source and clone are independently resumable.

A handoff records the goal/topic/scope, work done, decisions and reversals,
deliverables, verification and its limits, commits, still-open or deferred work,
and key facts needed next. Summaries describe historical work; they do not undo
filesystem changes or ask the agent to repeat completed tasks.

## What users and agents see

The extension patches Pi's native summary card in memory. The default card shows
the title, goal, outcome, messages/tool calls, recorded input/output/cache tokens,
and recorded inclusive cost. Ctrl+O or a fullscreen mouse click expands the full
report. Statistics describe unique recorded source entries, not new charges.
Parent totals include their children; do not add parent and child totals together.

For converted sessions, `/tree` opens a chronological containment outline:

```text
Orientation and architecture design (folded)
Specification and examples (folded)
Implementation campaign (open)
  Step 3 execution and verification (folded)
    Earlier completed subphases...
  [current] Branch and worktree cleanup (open)
    user: ...
    assistant: ...
```

Enter or Space folds/unfolds a group. `r` resumes **after its handoff**. Enter on
an original message uses Pi's normal navigation. `/` searches and reveals matching
descendants; Escape clears the search or closes the selector. F2 switches to the
raw native conversation graph, including its original labels and filters.
Containment is distinct from context ancestry: a child displayed under a phase
can be resumed at its historical point, before that phase's final handoff existed.

The agent receives the **full selected handoff text**, never the collapsed UI
placeholder. Navigator-owned projected summaries become honest work-context
messages, without Pi's alternative-branch preamble. Native persisted summaries
remain available to Pi and exports. With the extension unloaded, Pi's stock card
and model conversion apply. Independent history-mirroring providers may rebuild
from persisted records rather than this context hook; that provider behavior
needs separate live validation.

Native rendering and tree patches are guarded, session-scoped and reversible.
An incompatible host falls back to native rendering. They do not patch installed
files or require a different Pi-Bolt build.

## Parent context policy

Choose `parentHandoffMode` in global or trusted-project `tree-navigator.json`:

```json
{ "parentHandoffMode": "full" }
```

- `full` (default): keep the parent's own report and its completed child handoffs
  once each in child order, recursively. Children retain historical states;
  the parent report explains the later outcome and superseding decisions.
- `synthesized`: keep only the parent's relevance-focused report. Child reports
  stay in the archived history. The parent may need a longer report; live parent
  summaries have no fixed 4,000-character cap. Preserve what remains relevant
  rather than repeatedly squeezing every phase into the same length.

A valid trusted-project value overrides the global value. Invalid values warn
and fall back to the other valid layer, then `full`. The chosen policy is frozen
in each handoff. Changing the setting does not silently rewrite old context.
A retrospective plan has its own default policy and optional per-group override.

Synthesis is not a mechanical truncation. For retrospective conversion, provide
a reviewed parent report informed by the child reports. The converter does not
make model calls or establish that the report's claims are true.

## Workflow

1. Inspect the source to obtain its hash and stable entry IDs.
2. Derive a heuristic tree locally, optionally refine it with a model, and review
   the resulting nested range/report plan.
3. Preview the groups, handoffs, context policies and descendant session list.
4. Review every report, then create the clone. Creation does not switch sessions
   or send a provider request.

### Inside Pi

```text
/anchor clone inspect /absolute/path/to/session.jsonl
/anchor clone propose /absolute/path/to/session.jsonl
/anchor clone propose /absolute/path/to/session.jsonl --llm
/anchor clone propose /absolute/path/to/session.jsonl --model openai/gpt-6-luna:high
/anchor clone preview /absolute/path/to/plan.json
/anchor clone create /absolute/path/to/plan.json
```

`inspect` without a path inspects the current persisted session. Inspection and
preview use readable, searchable frames with counts, phase titles and warnings.
Press `j` for an explicit raw-JSON viewer; edits in that viewer are ignored.
`create` requires an idle UI session, preview review and confirmation. No command
appends preview content to the source. Quoted paths support spaces.

`propose` without a path uses the current session. It derives names, titles and
nesting from existing labels, user turns and rewind summaries. Where completion
is not established, heuristic groups stay open rather than inventing a report.
The model receives that baseline and the permitted textual history to refine
markers, labels, nesting, goals, outcomes and completed handoffs.

Inspection can report an in-progress source. Proposals, preview and creation
require completed recorded tool batches; known unfinished calls are rejected
before any model request rather than charging for an unusable plan.

Model analysis requires explicit `--llm` or `--model` and a disclosure/charge
confirmation. It uses Pi's model registry and existing credentials without
switching the current session model. The default model and thinking level are
the current session's; `provider/model:thinking` overrides both for the side call.
Escape cancels generation. No clone is created by proposing a tree.

The proposal shows a readable tree outline with goals, outcomes, reports and
analysis usage. Enter or `s` saves it; Escape cancels without saving. `e` explicitly
opens the raw JSON plan editor for advanced changes; invalid edits are refused.
Accepted plans are saved as new `0600` files in the source's
`.tree-clone-plans/` directory, or the explicit `--output <plan.json>` path.
Existing files are never overwritten. Source changes during generation require
a new proposal. Preview and clone confirmation are separate steps.

### Proposal input and model configuration

Global and trusted-project `tree-navigator.json` accept:

```json
{
  "treeProposal": {
    "model": "openai/gpt-6-luna:high",
    "tools": {
      "bash": "calls-only",
      "read": "omit",
      "grep": "full"
    }
  }
}
```

- With no configured model, or `"model": "current"`, use the current session
  model and thinking level. A selector without `:thinking` reuses the current
  thinking level, clamped to the target model's supported levels. An explicit
  unsupported thinking level is rejected. No model is selected or contacted for
  heuristic-only proposals.
- Full textual history is the default, including archived branches, assistant
  text/thinking, tool arguments/results, existing reports, labels and markers.
  Image/binary content and opaque signatures are omitted and reported.
- `full` includes a tool's textual call and result; `calls-only` retains arguments
  but omits result bodies/details; `omit` removes arguments and results. Exact
  tool names are matched through tool-call IDs; minimal graph metadata remains.
  The `bash` rule also covers native `!`/`!!` shell records and their context edits.
- Tool rules merge per name across trusted layers. Command flags
  `--omit-tool <name>`, `--calls-only-tool <name>` and `--full-tool <name>` override
  that request. Model selection can be overridden with `--model`.
- Invalid disclosure settings block model requests rather than silently sending
  more history. Untrusted project configuration is never read.
- These rules filter structured tool records, not copies already quoted in user
  messages, assistant prose or historical summaries. Review sensitive history
  before authorizing a provider request.

A history that fits the model's budget is refined directly in one request.
Large histories use multiple bounded requests and hierarchical consolidation;
permitted textual records are not silently truncated. Consolidation is limited
to three rounds and must reduce evidence size by at least 25% per round;
otherwise it stops with an explicit heuristic fallback and recorded usage.
An outline that cannot fit the selected model is rejected before any model request. Progress and proposal
usage are reported separately from the source session's historical accounting.
Provider failures, malformed output, unknown entry IDs or unsafe generated graph
cuts produce an explicit heuristic fallback; cancellation does not save a plan.
Model output cannot replace the source path/hash, and every proposed range passes
the deterministic converter's integrity checks before saving. Summary accuracy
still requires human review.

### Offline CLI

From this checkout with installed dependencies and Node 22.19+:
Use `node scripts/restructure-session.mjs --help` or `<command> --help` for syntax,
flags and the distinction between offline operations and paid model analysis.

```bash
node scripts/restructure-session.mjs inspect /path/to/session.jsonl
node scripts/restructure-session.mjs propose /path/to/session.jsonl --output /path/to/plan.json
node scripts/restructure-session.mjs propose /path/to/session.jsonl --model openai/gpt-6-luna:high --calls-only-tool bash --output /path/to/plan.json
node scripts/restructure-session.mjs preview /path/to/plan.json
node scripts/restructure-session.mjs create /path/to/plan.json <preview-token>
```

Success prints JSON; failure prints an error and exits nonzero. Preview writes
nothing. Its token binds the normalized plan, source bytes, descendant membership
and hashes, and reviewed descendant plans. Any change requires a new preview.

CLI `propose` prints the proposal, outline, warnings and observed analysis usage;
`--output` also saves its plan. Explicit `--llm`/`--model` authorizes provider
requests without an interactive dialog. The CLI reads global proposal settings
only; use flags for project-specific rules. Its default model/thinking comes from
the source's recorded state when the global model is absent/current. A standalone
CLI may not have providers registered by interactive extensions; select a model
available in its registry. Other CLI operations remain offline.

## Plan

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "source": "./original.jsonl",
  "sourceSha256": "<SHA-256 from inspect>",
  "nameSuffix": " (restructured)",
  "parentHandoffMode": "full",
  "recurse": false,
  "groups": [
    {
      "name": "implementation",
      "title": "Implementation campaign",
      "state": "open",
      "firstEntryId": "<phase start>",
      "lastEntryId": "<current tail>",
      "children": [
        {
          "name": "parser",
          "title": "Parser implementation",
          "state": "folded",
          "mode": "full",
          "firstEntryId": "<first included entry>",
          "lastEntryId": "<last included entry>",
          "goal": "Parse the input dialect.",
          "outcome": "Parser delivered and regression-tested.",
          "summary": "## Goal\n...\n\n## Delivered\n...\n\n## Decisions\n...\n\n## Rejected or Superseded\n...\n\n## Verification\n...\n\n## Commits\n...\n\n## Open or Deferred\n...\n\n## Key Facts\n..."
        },
        {
          "name": "current-tests",
          "title": "Integration tests",
          "state": "open",
          "firstEntryId": "<next work starts here>",
          "lastEntryId": "<current tail>"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- Ranges are inclusive IDs in append order, not line numbers. Siblings are ordered
  and disjoint; children fit inside their parent. Gaps stay verbatim. Open ranges
  can annotate existing graph regions without flattening them. Folded ranges
  require a single external incoming parent; rewinds inside that region are allowed.
  A cut with unrelated incoming branches is refused instead of silently rewired.
- Names are unique kebab-case, at most 40 characters. Reserved labels cannot be
  reused. Titles may be readable prose.
- `state` defaults to `folded`. Folded groups require non-empty reviewed reports.
  Open groups keep their raw history and completed child handoffs; an open child
  requires an open parent. `[current]` follows the current enclosing open group.
- `mode` overrides the plan's `parentHandoffMode`. The plan defaults to `full`.
- `goal` and `outcome` are optional display facts; otherwise they are extracted
  from report headings. Do not invent them when the history does not establish them.
- Child reports are inserted in chronological child order after the parent's own
  final report. Raw messages remain on their archived branches. This is an ordered
  handoff bundle, not a verbatim chronological interleaving of every parent sentence.
- Nesting is limited to 32 levels. Heuristic proposals keep deeper history raw
  inside the last supported open phase and report the annotation-depth limit.
  Every generated/saved plan passes schema parsing. Unknown fields are rejected.
- Relative `source` and `descendantPlans` paths resolve from the plan file.

## Descendant session families

Creation **copies descendant session histories unchanged by default**, including
nested worker/reviewer sessions. Each copy gets a new header ID/timestamp and its
`parentSession` points to its copied parent. Transcript bodies, including names,
usage and custom records, remain byte-identical. The root clone inherits the
source's `parentSession`: it is a sibling if the source has a parent, otherwise
it remains top-level. Source provenance is recorded separately.

Discovery follows actual canonical file-path links. It scans the source directory
and, for a conventional `sessions/--project--/` store, its sibling encoded project
directories. It does not search the whole filesystem or infer relationships from
agent names. Missing external sidecars and provider histories are not copied.

Opt into restructuring the descendants too using the plan:

```json
{
  "recurse": true,
  "descendantPlans": ["./worker-plan.json", "./reviewer-plan.json"]
}
```

Each descendant needs its own reviewed plan and source hash. The converter refuses
missing plans rather than silently treating recursive work as done. Root and child
plans use the same supported-input rules; already-branched descendants can still
be copied unchanged, and restructuring one uses the same graph-safety rules.
No automatic analysis or paid model requests are triggered by `recurse`.

## Integrity and limits

- Inspection and restructuring accept version-3 native session trees. Parents
  must precede children; duplicate IDs, missing targets and invalid references
  are refused. Existing rewind ancestry, summary `fromId` references (including
  Pi's `root` sentinel), labels and archived histories remain intact. New folds
  redirect continuations only at their explicit boundaries.
- Ordinary descendant copying preserves bodies without trying to restructure them.
- Every original entry ID/payload/timestamp/accounting record is retained inside
  its cloned session. Synthetic reports do not claim additional model usage.
- Compactions keep their original summary and retained-entry reference. Unsafe
  crossed boundaries are rejected even on archived branches. No compaction may
  hide newly created handoffs on the final active path. Open-only annotations do
  not invalidate an unchanged original compaction.
- Context edits stay with their targets across folds. Tool calls stay with their
  results. Orphan results, duplicate outstanding call IDs and unfinished source
  tool batches are refused for restructuring.
- Model/thinking state, system sections and tool declarations are restored and
  checked at original positions and summary continuations. Incompatible plain
  system-text replacements are refused.
- Original assistant usage still contributes to historical billing. While this
  extension is loaded, those pre-conversion measurements are invalidated as live
  context-size baselines, including Pi's native pre-request estimate. New assistant
  turns supply fresh measurements; no recorded usage is erased from the files.
- New files are staged with `0600` permissions and flushed before exclusive
  publication. Root context is checked by reopening through Pi. Source/family
  hashes and membership are checked before publishing. Failures roll back only
  the new files from that attempt; original files are never opened for writing.
- Each file publishes atomically; a process crash halfway through a multi-file
  family is not a filesystem-wide transaction. Parent/source paths in remaining
  copies still do not modify or reparent the original family.
- POSIX publication syncs containing directories. Post-publication temporary-file
  cleanup or sync failures are reported with the successful output paths.
- Pause activity while reviewing and creating a snapshot. Later source activity
  does not propagate to an existing clone.
- Extension custom state remains historical. Worker processes, external provider
  sessions and filesystem work are not recreated by copying their session records.

Resume the untouched original to go back. Use Pi's session-management UI to remove
unwanted clones. A conversion never replaces the original in place.

    readLedger: () => options.ledger,
    applyUserOps: () => ({ applied: [], rejected: [] }),
  };
  const pi = {
    registerCommand(name: string, commandOptions: Registered) {
      commands.push({ name, options: commandOptions });
    },
  } as unknown as ExtensionAPI;
  registerAnchorCommand(pi, deps);

  const width = options.width ?? 80;
  const screens = [...(options.screens ?? [])];
  const rendered: string[][] = [];
  const notifications: { message: string; type?: string }[] = [];
  const editors: string[] = [];
  const theme = {
    fg: (_color: string, text: string) => text,
    bold: (text: string) => text,
    italic: (text: string) => text,
  };
  const ctx = {
    cwd: options.cwd ?? tmpdir(),
    hasUI: options.hasUI ?? true,
    isIdle: () => true,
    sessionManager: Object.assign(
      SessionManager.inMemory(options.cwd ?? tmpdir()),
      { getSessionFile: () => options.sessionFile },
    ),
    ui: {
      notify(message: string, type?: string) {
        notifications.push({ message, type });
      },
      async editor(title: string) {
        editors.push(title);
        return undefined;
      },
      async confirm() {
        return false;
      },
      async input() {
        return (options.inputs ?? []).shift();
      },
      custom(
        factory: (
          tui: unknown,
          theme: unknown,
          keyboard: unknown,
          done: (result: unknown) => void,
        ) => Screen & { render(width: number): string[] },
      ) {
        const script = screens.shift();
        assert.ok(script, "unexpected extra screen");
        return new Promise((resolve) => {
          const tui = {
            terminal: { rows: 40, columns: width },
            requestRender() {},
          };
          const screen = factory(tui, theme, undefined, resolve);
          const lines = screen.render(width);
          rendered.push(lines);
          script(screen, lines);
        });
      },
    },
  } as unknown as ExtensionCommandContext;

  const command = commands[0]?.options;
  return {
    commands,
    command,
    ctx,
    calls,
    rendered,
    notifications,
    editors,
    run: (args: string) => command.handler(args, ctx),
    remainingScreens: () => screens.length,
  };
}

export type AutoNavigateDecision =

  "Decide whether a clear milestone was reached since the last anchor, or whether completed work should now be collapsed via rewind.",
  "Return JSON only with one of these shapes:",

  const candidate = fenced ? fenced[1].trim() : trimmed;
  try {
    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(candidate);
    if (
      typeof parsed === "object" &&
      parsed !== null &&
      !Array.isArray(parsed)

      return parsed as Record<string, unknown>;

  } catch {
    const start = candidate.indexOf("{");

    if (start >= 0 && end > start) {

export async function evaluateAutoNavigateTurn(options: {

          ? parsed.target_entry_id.trim()

      const newLabel =

        typeof parsed.summary_focus === "string"

          : "";

/**
 * Readable text for the `/anchor clone` screens: inspect, preview, plan outline
 * and the create confirmation.
 *
 * Pure: every function returns plain text lines bounded by a column width and
 * never JSON. Session names, titles and summaries are untrusted and sanitized.
 */
import {
  truncateToWidth,
  visibleWidth,
  wrapTextWithAnsi,
} from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";
import { sanitizeTerminalText } from "./frame.ts";
import type { RetrospectivePreview } from "./retrospective.ts";
import type {
  inspectRetrospectiveSession,
  RetrospectiveGroup,
  RetrospectivePlan,
} from "./retrospective-plan.ts";

/** What `inspectRetrospectiveSession` resolves with. */
export type InspectResult = Awaited<
  ReturnType<typeof inspectRetrospectiveSession>
>;

/** Source facts that turn ids into counts and titles; what is absent is left out of the text. */
export interface ViewContext {
  /** Entry id to its position in the source file. */
  readonly entryIndex?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>;
  /** Group name to its plan title. */
  readonly titles?: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
}

/** Facts about a proposal that the plan itself does not carry. */
export interface OutlineInfo {
  readonly sessionName: string;
  readonly entries: number;
  readonly method: "heuristic" | "model";
  readonly calls: number;
  readonly cost: number;
  readonly warnings: readonly string[];
}

interface ViewGroup {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly title?: string;
  readonly depth: number;
  readonly state: "folded" | "open";
  readonly mode: "full" | "synthesized";
  readonly firstEntryId: string;
  readonly lastEntryId: string;
  readonly summary: string;
}

const LABEL_WIDTH = 10;
const TAG_WIDTH = 8;
const ANCHOR_PREFIX = "anchor:";

const oneLine = (text: string): string =>
  sanitizeTerminalText(text).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
const plural = (count: number, one: string, many = `${one}s`): string =>
  `${count} ${count === 1 ? one : many}`;
const shortHash = (sha256: string): string => sha256.slice(0, 12);
const humanize = (name: string): string => name.replaceAll("-", " ");

/** `first` then `text` wrapped so continuation lines align under the text. */
function hanging(first: string, text: string, width: number): string[] {
  const hang = " ".repeat(visibleWidth(first));
  const room = Math.max(1, width - hang.length);
  return wrapTextWithAnsi(oneLine(text), room).map(
    (line, index) => (index === 0 ? first : hang) + line,
  );
}

const field = (label: string, text: string, width: number): string[] =>
  hanging(label.padEnd(LABEL_WIDTH), text, width);

const warning = (text: string, width: number): string[] =>
  hanging("! ", text, width);

/** First wrapped line of a text, ending in an ellipsis when more follows. */
function excerpt(first: string, text: string, width: number): string[] {
  const [head, ...rest] = hanging(first, text, width);
  if (rest.length === 0) return head ? [head] : [];
  return [`${truncateToWidth(head, Math.max(1, width - 1), "")}…`];
}

function fit(lines: readonly string[], width: number): string[] {
  return lines.map((line) => truncateToWidth(line.trimEnd(), width, "…"));
}

function stateCounts(
  groups: readonly { readonly state: "folded" | "open" }[],
): string {
  const folded = groups.filter((group) => group.state === "folded").length;
  return [
    folded > 0 && `${folded} folded`,
    groups.length - folded > 0 && `${groups.length - folded} open`,
  ]
    .filter((part): part is string => typeof part === "string")
    .join(", ");
}

function modeSummary(groups: readonly ViewGroup[]): string {
  const modes = ["full", "synthesized"] as const;
  const counts = modes
    .map((mode) => ({
      mode,
      count: groups.filter((group) => group.mode === mode).length,
    }))
    .filter(({ count }) => count > 0);
  if (counts.length === 0) return "none";
  if (counts.length === 1) return counts[0].mode;
  return `mixed (${counts.map(({ mode, count }) => `${count} ${mode}`).join(", ")})`;
}

function entryCount(
  group: ViewGroup,
  context: ViewContext,
): string | undefined {
  const first = context.entryIndex?.get(group.firstEntryId);
  const last = context.entryIndex?.get(group.lastEntryId);
  return first === undefined || last === undefined || last < first
    ? undefined
    : plural(last - first + 1, "entry", "entries");
}

/** The groups as an indented tree: state tag, title, entry count and a one-line summary excerpt. */
function groupLines(
  groups: readonly ViewGroup[],
  width: number,
  context: ViewContext,
): string[] {
  const mixed = new Set(groups.map((group) => group.mode)).size > 1;
  const lines: string[] = [];
  for (const group of groups) {
    const indent = " ".repeat(
      Math.min(2 + group.depth * 2, Math.max(2, width - 24)),
    );
    const tag = `[${group.state}]`.padEnd(TAG_WIDTH);
    const title =
      group.title ?? context.titles?.get(group.name) ?? humanize(group.name);
    const meta = [entryCount(group, context), mixed ? group.mode : undefined]
      .filter((part): part is string => part !== undefined)
      .join(", ");
    lines.push(
      ...hanging(
        `${indent}${tag} `,
        meta ? `${title} (${meta})` : title,
        width,
      ),
    );
    lines.push(
      ...excerpt(`${indent}${" ".repeat(TAG_WIDTH + 1)}`, group.summary, width),
    );
  }
  return lines;
}

function flattenPlan(plan: RetrospectivePlan): ViewGroup[] {
  const groups: ViewGroup[] = [];
  const visit = (children: readonly RetrospectiveGroup[], depth: number) => {
    for (const group of children) {
      groups.push({
        name: group.name,
        title: group.title === undefined ? undefined : oneLine(group.title),
        depth,
        state: group.state,
        mode: group.mode ?? plan.parentHandoffMode,
        firstEntryId: group.firstEntryId,
        lastEntryId: group.lastEntryId,
        summary: group.summary,
      });
      visit(group.children, depth + 1);
    }
  };
  visit(plan.groups, 0);
  return groups;
}

/** Position of every entry id in the source file, for entry counts. */
export function entryIndex(
  entries: readonly { readonly id: string }[],
): ReadonlyMap<string, number> {
  return new Map(entries.map((entry, index) => [entry.id, index]));
}

/** Group name to title for every titled group of a plan, however deeply nested. */
export function planTitles(
  plan: RetrospectivePlan,
): ReadonlyMap<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    flattenPlan(plan).flatMap(({ name, title }) =>
      title === undefined ? [] : [[name, title] as const],
    ),
  );
}

/** Session facts, graph shape, anchors and any unfinished tool calls. */
export function formatInspect(
  inspected: InspectResult,
  width: number,
): string[] {
  const { graph, pendingToolCalls } = inspected;
  const anchors = graph.labels.flatMap(({ label }) =>
    label?.startsWith(ANCHOR_PREFIX) ? [label.slice(ANCHOR_PREFIX.length)] : [],
  );
  const branches = graph.linear
    ? "1, linear history"
    : `${plural(graph.leaves.length, "branch", "branches")}, ${plural(graph.branchingPoints.length, "fork point")}`;
  const lines = [
    ...field("Session", inspected.name, width),
    ...field("Id", inspected.sessionId, width),
    ...field(
      "Entries",
      `${inspected.entries} · ${plural(inspected.turns.length, "user turn")}`,
      width,
    ),
    ...field("Branches", branches, width),
    ...field(
      "Folds",
      graph.summaries.length
        ? plural(graph.summaries.length, "fold summary", "fold summaries")
        : "none",
      width,
    ),
    ...field(
      "Anchors",
      anchors.length ? `${anchors.length}: ${anchors.join(", ")}` : "none",
      width,
    ),
    ...field(
      "Tools",
      pendingToolCalls.length
        ? `${pendingToolCalls.length} unfinished`
        : "all calls finished",
      width,
    ),
    ...field("Hash", shortHash(inspected.sourceSha256), width),
    ...field("File", inspected.source, width),
  ];
  if (pendingToolCalls.length) {
    lines.push(
      "",
      ...warning(
        `Unfinished tool calls: ${pendingToolCalls.join(", ")}. Wait for their results before proposing or cloning.`,
        width,
      ),
    );
  }
  return fit(lines, width);
}

/** The new session, its groups as a tree, the handoff mode, descendant sessions and warnings. */
export function formatPreview(
  preview: RetrospectivePreview,
  width: number,
  context: ViewContext = {},
): string[] {
  const groups: ViewGroup[] = preview.groups.map((group) => ({
    ...group,
    title: undefined,
  }));
  const copied = preview.descendants.filter(
    ({ mode }) => mode === "copied",
  ).length;
  const restructured = preview.descendants.length - copied;
  const family = preview.descendants.length
    ? `${plural(preview.descendants.length, "descendant session")}: ${copied} copied unchanged, ${restructured} restructured`
    : "none";
  const lines = [
    ...field("New", preview.name, width),
    ...field("From", preview.source, width),
    ...field("Hash", shortHash(preview.sourceSha256), width),
    ...field(
      "Entries",
      `${preview.originalEntries} original + ${preview.addedEntries} added`,
      width,
    ),
    ...field(
      "Groups",
      groups.length ? `${groups.length}: ${stateCounts(groups)}` : "none",
      width,
    ),
    ...field("Handoff", modeSummary(groups), width),
    ...field("Family", family, width),
  ];
  if (groups.length)
    lines.push("", "Outline", ...groupLines(groups, width, context));
  for (const text of preview.warnings) lines.push("", ...warning(text, width));
  return fit(lines, width);
}

/** A proposal at a glance: session, method and cost, then the proposed tree and any warnings. */
export function formatPlanOutline(
  plan: RetrospectivePlan,
  info: OutlineInfo,
  width: number,
  context: ViewContext = {},
): string[] {
  const groups = flattenPlan(plan);
  const method = info.calls
    ? `${info.method} · ${plural(info.calls, "model request")} · $${info.cost.toFixed(4)}`
    : `${info.method} · no model requests`;
  const lines = [
    ...field(
      "Session",
      `${info.sessionName} · ${plural(info.entries, "entry", "entries")}`,
      width,
    ),
    ...field("Method", method, width),
    ...field(
      "Groups",
      groups.length ? `${groups.length}: ${stateCounts(groups)}` : "none",
      width,
    ),
    ...field("Handoff", modeSummary(groups), width),
  ];
  if (groups.length)
    lines.push("", "Outline", ...groupLines(groups, width, context));
  for (const text of info.warnings) lines.push("", ...warning(text, width));
  return fit(lines, width);
}

/** Right-hand badge of the inspect screen. */
export const inspectBadge = (inspected: InspectResult): string =>
  plural(inspected.entries, "entry", "entries");

/** Right-hand badge of the preview screen. */
export const previewBadge = (preview: RetrospectivePreview): string =>
  `${plural(preview.groups.length, "group")} · +${preview.addedEntries} entries`;

/** Right-hand badge of the proposal screen. */
export const outlineBadge = (
  plan: RetrospectivePlan,
  info: OutlineInfo,
): string => `${info.method} · ${plural(flattenPlan(plan).length, "group")}`;

/** Body of the final confirmation dialog; the dialog wraps it itself. */
export function formatCreateConfirmation(
  preview: RetrospectivePreview,
): string {
  const groups = preview.groups.length
    ? `${plural(preview.groups.length, "group")} (${stateCounts(preview.groups)})`
    : "no groups";
  const copied = preview.descendants.filter(
    ({ mode }) => mode === "copied",
  ).length;
  const lines = [
    `From ${oneLine(preview.source)}`,
    `Adds ${plural(preview.addedEntries, "entry", "entries")} to the ${preview.originalEntries} original: ${groups}.`,
  ];
  if (preview.descendants.length) {
    lines.push(
      `${plural(preview.descendants.length, "descendant session")}: ${copied} copied unchanged, ${preview.descendants.length - copied} restructured.`,
    );
  }
  lines.push(
    "The original session will remain untouched, and Pi stays in the current session.",
  );
  return lines.join("\n");
}

/**
 * Tests for the local `estimateContextTokens` helper.
 *
 * The helper is a drop-in replacement for the `pi-agent-core` export that
 * pi 1.0.0 removed; it delegates the per-message math to the host's public
 * `estimateTokens`, so the table below pins the *semantics* that matters
 * (usage baseline + trailing estimates, invalid-usage fall-through,
 * per-message message shapes) without claiming cross-version numeric
 * parity — see `context-tokens.ts` file JSDoc.
 */

import * as assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { describe, it } from "node:test";
import type { AgentMessage } from "@earendil-works/pi-agent-core";
import { estimateTokens } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
import { estimateContextTokens } from "./context-tokens.ts";

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Fixtures — chars/4 means every token value below is an exact multiple of 4
// chars per token, so the expectations stay readable.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

const text = (chars: number) => "x".repeat(chars);

function user(chars: number): AgentMessage {
  return {
    role: "user",
    content: [{ type: "text", text: text(chars) }],
    timestamp: 1,
  } as unknown as AgentMessage;
}

function userWithImage(textChars: number): AgentMessage {
  return {
    role: "user",
    content: [
      { type: "text", text: text(textChars) },
      // estimateTokens accounts every image block as 4800 chars → 1200 tokens.
      { type: "image", data: "AAAA", mimeType: "image/png" },
    ],
    timestamp: 1,
  } as unknown as AgentMessage;
}

function assistant(
  chars: number,
  opts: { totalTokens?: number; stopReason?: string } = {},
): AgentMessage {
  return {
    role: "assistant",
    content: [{ type: "text", text: text(chars) }],
    api: "anthropic",
    provider: "test",
    model: "test",
    stopReason: opts.stopReason ?? "endTurn",
    timestamp: 1,
    usage: {
      input: 0,
      output: 0,
      cacheRead: 0,
      cacheWrite: 0,
      totalTokens: opts.totalTokens ?? 0,
      cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, total: 0 },
    },
  } as unknown as AgentMessage;
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Estimator table
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

describe("estimateContextTokens", () => {
  it("empty message list is 0", () => {
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens([]), 0);
  });

  it("no usage anywhere: sums estimateTokens over every message", () => {
    const chain = [
      user(4), //     1
      assistant(8), // 2
      user(400), //  100
    ];
    assert.equal(
      estimateContextTokens(chain),
      estimateTokens(chain[0]) +
        estimateTokens(chain[1]) +
        estimateTokens(chain[2]),
    );
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens(chain), 103);
  });

  it("uses the newest valid assistant usage as baseline + trailing estimates", () => {
    const chain = [
      user(4), //                          ignored (before the baseline)
      assistant(8, { totalTokens: 1000 }), // baseline 1000, content not re-counted
      user(400), //                         trailing 100
      user(400), //                         trailing 100
    ];
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens(chain), 1000 + 100 + 100);
  });

  it("picks the newest valid usage, not the oldest", () => {
    const chain = [
      assistant(4, { totalTokens: 1000 }), // older valid usage — must be ignored
      user(400), //                           covered by the newest baseline
      assistant(4, { totalTokens: 2000 }), // newest valid baseline
      user(400), //                           trailing: 100
    ];
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens(chain), 2000 + 100);
  });

  it("skips aborted/error/zero-usage baselines and falls through to the previous valid usage", () => {
    const chain = [
      user(4), //                                       ignored
      assistant(4, { totalTokens: 1000 }), //           baseline 1000 (endTurn)
      user(400), //                                      trailing 100
      assistant(400, { totalTokens: 900, stopReason: "aborted" }), // trailing 100
      assistant(400, { totalTokens: 800, stopReason: "error" }), //   trailing 100
      assistant(400, { totalTokens: 0 }), // zero usage → trailing 100
      user(400), //                                      trailing 100
    ];
    // A regression that took the newest usage regardless of stopReason
    // would return 0 + 100, or 800 + 200 when only zero-usage was skipped.
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens(chain), 1000 + 100 * 5);
  });

  it("counts toolResult / custom / branchSummary shapes", () => {
    const toolResult = {
      role: "toolResult",
      toolCallId: "tc-1",
      toolName: "read",
      content: [{ type: "text", text: text(400) }],
      isError: false,
      timestamp: 1,
    } as unknown as AgentMessage;
    const custom = {
      role: "custom",
      customType: "note",
      content: [{ type: "text", text: text(400) }],
      display: false,
      timestamp: 1,
    } as unknown as AgentMessage;
    const branchSummary = {
      role: "branchSummary",
      summary: text(400),
      fromId: "entry-1",
      timestamp: 1,
    } as unknown as AgentMessage;

    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens([toolResult]), 100);
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens([custom]), 100);
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens([branchSummary]), 100);
    assert.equal(
      estimateContextTokens([toolResult, custom, branchSummary]),
      300,
    );
  });

  it("system message: delegates to the host estimateTokens (0.84.2 scores 0; 1.0.0 counts content+sections+toolsAdded)", () => {
    const system = {
      role: "system",
      content: [{ type: "text", text: text(400) }],
      sections: { appended: text(400) },
      toolsAdded: [{ name: "navigate_tree", description: text(400) }],
      timestamp: 1,
    } as unknown as AgentMessage;

    // Host-semantics pin, not a cross-version number: pi 1.0.0's
    // estimateTokens counts a system message's content + sections +
    // toolsAdded, while pre-1.0 hosts have no system case and return 0.
    // Asserting delegation keeps the unit suite correct on both hosts and
    // documents the divergence instead of pinning a false parity.
    const hostSystemTokens = estimateTokens(system);
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens([system]), hostSystemTokens);
    assert.equal(
      estimateContextTokens([user(400), system]),
      100 + hostSystemTokens,
    );
  });

  it("counts the effective system state once after section replacement", () => {
    const head = {
      role: "system" as const,
      content: "",
      sections: { context: "x".repeat(4000) },
      timestamp: 0,
    };
    const update = {
      role: "system" as const,
      content: "",
      sections: { context: "tiny" },
      timestamp: 1,
    };
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens([head, user(4), update]), 2);
  });

  it("image blocks are accounted as chars in the trailing estimate", () => {
    // 400 text chars + 4800 image chars = 5200 → 1300 tokens.
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens([userWithImage(400)]), 1300);
  });

  it("circular toolCall arguments throw (plain JSON.stringify — no safeJsonStringify guard)", () => {
    const circular: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    circular.self = circular;
    const message = assistant(4, { totalTokens: 0 });
    (message as unknown as { content: unknown }).content = [
      { type: "toolCall", id: "tc", name: "x", arguments: circular },
    ];
    assert.throws(() => estimateContextTokens([message]), TypeError);
  });

  it("image blocks after the baseline are counted in the trailing estimate", () => {
    const chain = [
      assistant(4, { totalTokens: 500 }),
      userWithImage(400), // trailing 1300
    ];
    assert.equal(estimateContextTokens(chain), 500 + 1300);
  });
});

function validAssistantUsage(message: AgentMessage): Usage | undefined {
  if (message.role !== "assistant") return undefined;
  const assistant = message as {
    stopReason?: string;
    usage?: Usage;
  };
  if (
    assistant.stopReason !== "aborted" &&
    assistant.stopReason !== "error" &&
    assistant.usage &&
    calculateContextTokens(assistant.usage) > 0
  ) {
    return assistant.usage;
  }
  return undefined;
}

/** Split a baseline-safe projection into recorded usage and its estimated tail. */
export function splitContextEstimate(messages: AgentMessage[]): {
  baseline: number;
  tail: number;
} {
  const anchor = newestUsageIndex(messages);
  const usage = anchor >= 0 ? validAssistantUsage(messages[anchor]) : undefined;
  const currentSystem =
    anchor < 0 ? getCurrentSystemMessage(messages) : undefined;
  let tail = currentSystem ? estimateTokens(currentSystem) : 0;
  for (let j = anchor + 1; j < messages.length; j++) {
    if (anchor < 0 && messages[j].role === "system") continue;
    tail += estimateTokens(messages[j]);
  }
  return {
    baseline: usage ? calculateContextTokens(usage) : 0,
    tail,
  };
}

/** Find the newest valid usage in messages whose stale baselines have been invalidated. */
export function newestUsageIndex(messages: AgentMessage[]): number {
  for (let i = messages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    if (validAssistantUsage(messages[i])) return i;
  }
  return -1;
}

/** Compare projected content on one heuristic without historical usage baselines. */
export function estimateContentTokens(messages: AgentMessage[]): number {
  const system = getCurrentSystemMessage(messages);
  return (
    (system ? estimateTokens(system) : 0) +
    messages.reduce(
      (sum, message) =>
        sum + (message.role === "system" ? 0 : estimateTokens(message)),
      0,
    )
  );
}

/** Estimate request headroom conservatively against the SDK's denser text heuristic. */
export function estimateRequestTokens(messages: AgentMessage[]): number {
  const converted = convertToLlm(messages);
  const anchor = newestUsageIndex(converted);
  const usage =
    anchor >= 0 ? validAssistantUsage(converted[anchor]) : undefined;
  const tail = converted
    .slice(anchor + 1)
    .reduce((sum, message) => sum + estimateTokens(message), 0);
  const content = converted.reduce(
    (sum, message) => sum + estimateTokens(message),
    0,
  );
  // Host estimates use four chars/token; the SDK's text heuristic uses 3.5.
  return Math.max(
    Math.ceil((content * 8) / 7),
    (usage ? calculateContextTokens(usage) : 0) + Math.ceil((tail * 8) / 7),
  );
}

/** Estimate projected context with Pi's heuristic and the effective system state. */
export function estimateContextTokens(messages: AgentMessage[]): number {
  const { baseline, tail } = splitContextEstimate(messages);
  return baseline + tail;
}

/**
 * Rendering for the Session Continuity Ledger: the model-facing briefing, the
 * fold-time capture request with its `<continuity-delta>` schema, and a compact
 * UI summary.
 *
 * No I/O and no pi runtime imports.
 */

import {
  type ContinuityDelta,
  ContinuityError,
  capText,
  type ItemKind,
  isUserOrigin,
  type Ledger,
  type LedgerItem,
  parseDelta,
} from "./continuity-ledger.ts";

export const CONTINUITY_DELTA_TAG = "continuity-delta";
const DELTA_OPEN = `<${CONTINUITY_DELTA_TAG}>`;
const DELTA_CLOSE = `</${CONTINUITY_DELTA_TAG}>`;

export const estimateBriefingTokens = (text: string): number =>
  Math.ceil(text.length / 4);

const oneLine = (text: string): string => text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
const idNumber = (item: LedgerItem): number => Number(item.id.slice(1));
const byId = (a: LedgerItem, b: LedgerItem): number =>
  idNumber(a) - idNumber(b);

const SECTIONS: readonly { kind: ItemKind; title: string }[] = [
  { kind: "objective", title: "Objective" },
  { kind: "sub-goal", title: "Active goals" },
  { kind: "rule", title: "Binding rules" },
  { kind: "decision", title: "Decisions" },
  { kind: "steering", title: "Active steering" },
  { kind: "fact", title: "Facts" },
  { kind: "file", title: "Files" },
];

// Dropped oldest-first in this order. Objective, goals, rules, decisions and
// stale file pointers are never dropped.
const DROP_ORDER = ["fact", "file", "steering"] as const;
type Droppable = (typeof DROP_ORDER)[number];

export const isVisible = (item: LedgerItem): boolean =>
  item.status === "active" || (item.kind === "file" && item.status === "stale");

function renderItem(item: LedgerItem): string {
  if (item.kind === "file" && item.file) {
    const stale =
      item.status === "stale"
        ? " [STALE: file changed since it was pinned]"
        : "";
    return `${item.id} ${item.text} — ${oneLine(item.file.why)}${stale}`;
  }
  const tags = [
    item.scopeAnchor !== undefined && `@${item.scopeAnchor}`,
    // Items the user did not author are not binding on their own.
    (item.kind === "objective" ||
      item.kind === "rule" ||
      item.kind === "decision") &&
      !isUserOrigin(item.source.origin) &&
      !item.pinned &&
      item.source.origin,
  ].filter((tag): tag is string => typeof tag === "string");
  const prefix = tags.length > 0 ? ` [${tags.join(" ")}]` : "";
  const quote =
    item.quote !== undefined &&
    (item.kind === "rule" || item.kind === "decision")
      ? `\n  > "${oneLine(item.quote)}"`
      : "";
  return `${item.id}${prefix} ${oneLine(item.text)}${quote}`;
}

function plural(count: number, noun: string): string {
  return `${count} ${noun}${count === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
}

function omissionNote(omitted: Record<Droppable, number>): string | undefined {
  const parts = [
    omitted.fact > 0 && plural(omitted.fact, "fact"),
    omitted.file > 0 && plural(omitted.file, "file pointer"),
    omitted.steering > 0 && `${omitted.steering} steering`,
  ].filter((part): part is string => typeof part === "string");
  return parts.length > 0
    ? `[omitted for budget: ${parts.join(", ")}]`
    : undefined;
}

export interface BriefingOptions {
  readonly maxTokens: number;
}

export interface Briefing {
  readonly text: string;
  readonly estimatedTokens: number;
  /** True when the never-dropped items alone exceed `maxTokens`; they are returned anyway. */
  readonly overBudget: boolean;
  readonly omitted: Readonly<Record<Droppable, number>>;
}

function compose(
  ledger: Ledger,
  items: readonly LedgerItem[],
  omitted: Record<Droppable, number>,
): string {
  const lines = [`[navigate_tree continuity ledger rev ${ledger.rev}]`];
  for (const { kind, title } of SECTIONS) {
    const section = items.filter((item) => item.kind === kind).sort(byId);
    if (section.length === 0) continue;
    lines.push("", `${title}:`, ...section.map(renderItem));
  }
  if (items.length === 0) lines.push("", "(no active items)");
  const note = omissionNote(omitted);
  if (note) lines.push("", note);
  return lines.join("\n");
}

/**
 * Model-facing briefing, deterministic in kind order then id. Superseded, completed
 * and archived items are not rendered. Over budget, facts, then file pointers, then
 * steering are dropped oldest-first and the omission is stated in the text.
 */
export function renderBriefing(
  ledger: Ledger,
  { maxTokens }: BriefingOptions,
): Briefing {
  let shown = ledger.items.filter(isVisible);
  const omitted: Record<Droppable, number> = { fact: 0, file: 0, steering: 0 };
  let text = compose(ledger, shown, omitted);
  for (const kind of DROP_ORDER) {
    const candidates = shown
      .filter((item) => item.kind === kind && item.status !== "stale")
      .sort(byId);
    for (const victim of candidates) {
      if (estimateBriefingTokens(text) <= maxTokens) break;
      shown = shown.filter((item) => item !== victim);
      omitted[kind] += 1;
      text = compose(ledger, shown, omitted);
    }
  }
  const estimatedTokens = estimateBriefingTokens(text);
  return {
    text,
    estimatedTokens,
    overBudget: estimatedTokens > maxTokens,
    omitted,
  };
}

/** A user message the model may cite when it reports a supersession. */
export interface UserEntryRef {

const USER_REF_PREVIEW_CHARS = 160;

const DELTA_SCHEMA = `${DELTA_OPEN}
{
  "completed": ["S2"],
  "ratified": [
    { "kind": "decision", "text": "Use sqlite for the index", "quote": "go with sqlite" }
  ],
  "superseded": [
    { "ids": ["R3"], "with": { "kind": "rule", "text": "Use tabs", "quote": "actually, tabs" }, "citedEntryId": "<id of the later user message>" }
  ],
  "expiredSteering": ["T5"]

${DELTA_CLOSE}`;

/**

 * the span being folded, and how to report changes as a `<continuity-delta>`.
